rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Conspiracy, Duality, and the War for Attention", "body": "The conversation opened with a reaction to a clip of Joe Rogan warning that seeing conspiracy in everything was dangerous, and a host argued the remark made long-time students of hidden history look foolish. Chance said he believed the biggest conspiracy theory, at the bottom of the rabbit hole, was a relief, because nobody was in charge. Sam Tripoli said he did not think there was a center and that light and dark battled over attention. Chance replied that the center was everywhere, as the life force animating all matter, and that the real contest was over each person's own attention."}, {"title": "Astrotheology and the Technology of Language", "body": "Chance described his specialty as the technology of language, using etymology and philology to argue that spiritual traditions and mythologies trace back to the stars, a field the nineteenth century writer Robert Taylor called astrotheology. He recommended John McHugh's book The Celestial Code of Scripture, which he said traced Bible stories to wordplay in star names. Chance also offered his own reading of Christopher Columbus, suggesting the name meant carrier of the Christ and dove, and that the Santa Maria echoed ark mythology. He framed much of ancient history as astrotheology and described history as story."}, {"title": "The Green Language and Eve as Life", "body": "Chance described the green language, also called the language of the birds, as the practice of reading between the lines, noticing puns and wordplay, and holding left brain and right brain meanings together. He credited his friend Gabe of the Slick Dissident channel with the line that philology is lockpicking. As an example, Chance explained that he saw the four Hebrew letters of the divine name as having several possible English transliterations, one of which he read as Eve, a word he said meant life. He presented these as his interpretations of the symbolism rather than settled fact."}, {"title": "Biofield Tuning and the World as Mirror", "body": "Chance described Biofield Tuning as a way of using a tuning fork to find stuck energy in a person's energy field, which he said extended roughly six feet from the body and could be done remotely over video. He said distance from the body suggested when something happened in a person's life, and that stuck energy represented limiting beliefs and avoided feelings. Chance compared restoring that energy to soul retrieval. He also argued that events in a person's life mirrored their inner world, and that learning to read that symbolism worked as a kind of psychic self-defense."}, {"title": "Demons, the Demiurge, and Victim Consciousness", "body": "Asked about fallen angels and the demiurge, Chance said he did not believe in archons or a ruling demiurge and called that belief the ultimate form of victim consciousness. He described the demiurge as a misunderstanding of the old creator, preserver, and destroyer idea, and tied it to the Hercules constellation. Chance explained that he read demons philologically as divided parts of the self cut off from its source. On reincarnation, he said he did not know, called his ideas speculation, and said he preferred to focus on making this life as good as possible."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined host Sam Tripoli and the crew on Tin Foil Hat, episode 643, for a wide-ranging talk about astrotheology, philology, and Biofield Tuning. We also got into the green language, the demiurge, and what reincarnation might mean.
